interpretation: The queue API and worker stayed available during the 30-minute subset soak. This establishes runtime health and API latency for the current eligible subset; changing eligible match counts mean it is not a fixed-cohort throughput test.
Rolling-hour document and confirmed-link counts increased, but they do not prove profile-job throughput or full historical import completeness.

The shared source network gate used at most one of two slots during the soak. Most PBP queue rows wait for match indexing or player source IDs, so more network/browser slots do not resolve the dominant waiting state.

Flashscore CPU had bursts around its 1.5-vCPU quota, while median CPU was lower. The four-browser trial previously reached 1.553 GiB / 2 GiB and was rolled back; this soak does not justify raising slots.
PostgreSQL remained below its configured memory, CPU, connection, and lock limits. Redis and Collector are closer to their memory caps.
